newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank seen supporting lev after rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank seen supporting lev after rate cut.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev traded between 219-221 per dollar in the morning, firmer than 222-223 at Thursday's close as the central bank stepped in to support the currency after a in interest rate cut on Thursday, dealers said.
"The rate cut has not had a negative impact (on the lev) so far because of the central bank's active support for the lev near 219.50 per dollar," a dealer said.

The interbank market opened amid large volatility as the new rate came into effect with dollar bids at 220-221 levs and asks at 225-228 levs but central bank dollar offers quickly consolidated trade around 220 levs per dollar, dealers said.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) on Thursday cut the monthly central interest rate to 20 percent from 25 percent, or 240 percent annually from current 300 percent.
The rate was cut due to positive changes in the financial system, the BNB said without identifying them.

The BNB hiked rate on September 23 to the all-time high of 300 percent and put nine more banks under special supervision in a bid to stabilise the fragile lev and the shaky financial system. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
